exposure: Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis HN019 supplementation
cohort: 474 infants participated in a randomised, controlled, 3-arm trial, with mothers receiving intervention from 35 weeks gestation and infants from birth, and faecal samples collected from 650 instances within this group.
finding: L. rhamnosus HN001 probiotic supplementation reduced infant eczema risk by 50% and was associated with increased overall glycerol-3 phosphate transport capacity and enrichment of L. rhamnosus in the infant gut microbiota.
